title: How Long Does a Bank Wire Transfer Take?
summary: Wire transfer times vary by destination and bank. Domestic wires clear in one business day; international wires take 1 to 5 days.
body_markdown:
Sending a wire transfer sounds simple until you're watching the clock and wondering where your money is. Timing, cut-off windows, and the number of banks in the chain all play a role in how fast funds actually land. Knowing the rules ahead of time can save you a lot of stress.


**TL;DR:**


- Domestic wire transfers settle within 1 business day; same-bank transfers clear in minutes.
- International wires take 1 to 5 business days, with SWIFT fees averaging $25 to $65 per transfer.
- Submit before your bank's cut-off (Chase: 4 PM ET) or your transfer rolls to the next business day.
- One typo in routing details triggers immediate rejection; verify SWIFT codes and IBANs before sending.
- Dots routes $1.5 billion annually to over 1 million payees, cutting the delays that compound at scale.


## What Is a Wire Transfer?


A wire transfer moves funds electronically from one bank account to another across secure interbank networks. When estimating how long does a wire transfer take bank to bank, the timeline depends on the routing system. US institutions route domestic payments through Fedwire (Federal Reserve Wire Network) and CHIPS (Clearing House Interbank Payments System). For a deeper look at how these compare with other options, see[ACH payments vs wire transfers](https://usedots.com/blog/what-is-the-difference-between-wire-transfers-and-ach-payments/) . International payments rely on SWIFT (Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication), a global messaging network that connects over 11,000 financial institutions across[200+ countries](https://www.swift.com/) . SWIFT does not move money directly. It transmits standardized payment instructions between banks, which each process and settle independently. Payments may also pass through intermediary banks identified by their IBAN (International Bank Account Number) and SWIFT code before funds land. That multi-bank chain is what determines how long an international wire takes to land.


## How Long Do Domestic Wire Transfers Take?


When determining how long does a wire transfer take domestic, your submission window controls the timeline. For a full[wire vs ACH speed and cost comparison](https://usedots.com/blog/ach-wire-transfer-comparison/) , see our dedicated guide. Does a wire transfer happen immediately? Sometimes.


- Moving money between accounts at the same institution takes only minutes.
- When asking how long does a bank transfer take between different banks, expect settlement within hours. The Expedited Funds Availability Act mandates clearing within one business day for domestic wire transfers. That means funds must be available in the recipient's account by the next business day at the latest. Missing your bank's cut-off time, however, resets that clock: your transfer enters the queue the following morning instead.


## How Long Do International Wire Transfers Take?


When asking how long do[global wire transfers](https://usedots.com/blog/how-long-do-global-wire-transfers-take/) take internationally, expect a settlement window of[1 to 5 business days](https://www.gobankingrates.com/banking/technology/how-long-does-a-wire-transfer-take/) . This timeline changes based on the destination and the chain of intermediary banks.


If you wonder how long does a SWIFT (Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication) transfer take internationally, the answer depends on how many banks handle the message chain. Each intermediary bank queues, validates, and forwards the payment instructions independently, a process that can add hours or an entire business day per hop. Most transfers clear within 1 to 3 business days when routing is straightforward, but payments into developing markets or less-connected banking systems regularly reach the 4 to 5 business day end of that window. Weekends and public holidays in either country pause processing entirely, extending the total timeline further.

Your submission timing determines settlement speed. Cut-off times vary by bank and method: Chase closes at 4 PM ET; Wells Fargo online closes at 5 PM PT. Check your bank's exact window. Online submissions offer later windows than branch visits.

## Factors That Affect Wire Transfer Speed


Several variables determine how long a bank transfer takes between different banks. You cannot alter clearing networks, but managing submission timing prevents delays.


- Missing a domestic wire cut off time same day pushes your processing to the next business day. Understanding[what an ACH payment is](https://usedots.com/blog/what-is-ach-payment-how-does-it-work/) can help you choose a better-timed alternative.
- Wire networks pause on weekends. Cross-border payments must account for closures in sending and receiving countries.
- International payments route through one to three intermediary banks, and each hop adds independent queuing and validation time. Fewer intermediaries mean faster settlement; payments into less-connected banking systems regularly hit the higher end of the 1 to 5 business day window. Confirming the recipient's bank details (SWIFT code, IBAN, and account number) before you send reduces the chance of a routing error that forces the payment back through the chain.


## How Much Do Wire Transfers Cost?


A domestic wire transfer typically costs $0 to $35. Your exact bank of america wire transfer fee depends on whether you initiate the request online or at a physical branch. For[cross-border money transfers](https://usedots.com/blog/cross-border-money-transfer-guide/) , SWIFT international outgoing wire fees average[$25 to $65 per transfer](https://www.bankrate.com/banking/wire-transfer-fees/) .


That base price covers only what your bank charges to send the wire. For international transfers, each intermediary bank in the SWIFT chain typically deducts its own processing fee (between $10 and $35 per hop) before forwarding the funds, which means the recipient can land short of the full amount. Currency conversion adds another layer: banks apply their own FX rate on top of the mid-market rate, and that markup is rarely disclosed upfront. On high-volume payout operations, those compounding fees erode margins quickly.


## How to Track a Wire Transfer


A completed dashboard status only means the sending institution transmitted the instructions. Intermediary processing can still delay the receiving bank from crediting the account.


To trace missing funds, request the exact tracking code from your bank:


- For domestic payments, request the IMAD/OMAD number to locate the transaction within the clearing network.
- For a cross-border SWIFT transfer, ask for the UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference), a 36-character code assigned to every SWIFT payment at origination. Share it with your bank's wire operations team; they can use it to query the GPI (Global Payments Initiative) tracker and pinpoint exactly which intermediary is holding the funds. If a bank in the chain has flagged the payment for compliance review, this step surfaces that blockage immediately so you can act.


## How to Avoid Wire Transfer Delays


You control several variables that affect settlement speeds. A few preventative steps reduce the risk of stalled funds.


- Initiate transfers early to beat the domestic wire cut off time same day.
- Verify routing details. Double-check the recipient's legal name, account number, SWIFT code, and IBAN. One typo triggers an immediate rejection.
- Check for bank holidays in the sending and receiving countries. Local closures pause all interbank clearing activity.
- Submit payments online. Digital portals grant later deadlines than physical branches.
- Validate instructions with the recipient through a secondary channel to protect your business against payment fraud.


## Alternatives to Wire Transfers


When wire transfers cost too much or move too slowly, you have alternative routing options. The right choice depends on settlement speed, destination, and transaction size.


- [ACH payments for businesses](https://usedots.com/blog/how-ach-payments-work-business-guide/) : These batch-processed domestic payments clear in 1 to 3 business days. Banks process them cheaply, making them a poor fit for urgent deadlines.
- [RTP (Real-Time Payments)](https://usedots.com/blog/what-are-real-time-payments/) and FedNow are US instant payment rails that settle funds in seconds, any time of day, including weekends and holidays. Unlike wire transfers, they carry no cut-off windows and no SWIFT intermediary fees. They are best suited for domestic payouts where speed matters and wire costs are difficult to absorb.

Domestic wires can clear in hours, but international transfers take longer because SWIFT routes funds through multiple intermediary banks before the money lands. ## FAQs


### How long does a domestic wire transfer take at major banks like Chase, Wells Fargo, and Bank of America?


Domestic wire transfers at Chase, Wells Fargo, and Bank of America typically settle the same business day if you submit before the bank's cut-off time, which ranges from 2 PM to 6 PM local time depending on the institution and whether you submit online or at a branch. Missing that cut-off pushes processing to the next business day, so online submission is your best option for catching the latest possible deadline.


### How long does an international wire transfer take, and what slows it down?


International wire transfers through SWIFT generally take 1 to 5 business days, with the exact timeline depending on the destination country, the number of intermediary banks in the chain, and public holidays in both the sending and receiving countries. Each intermediary bank adds processing time, and cross-border payments that touch multiple currencies often carry additional FX conversion steps that extend settlement further.


### What's the fastest way to send high-volume payouts without hitting wire transfer cut-off times or SWIFT fees?


For businesses sending thousands of payouts, wire transfers compound the problem: SWIFT fees run $25 to $65 per transfer, cut-off windows push batches to the next day, and intermediary hops delay settlement. Dots routes payouts through RTP, FedNow, and 300+ local rails, settling funds in seconds by default with no instant-payout surcharge and no daily volume cap, which removes the structural bottlenecks that wire transfers build into high-volume payout operations.


### Does a wire transfer happen immediately, or is there always a delay?


Wire transfers are not always instant. Transfers between accounts at the same bank often clear within minutes, but bank-to-bank domestic wires depend on submission timing relative to the cut-off window and can take several hours to one business day. International wires routed through SWIFT add 1 to 5 business days due to intermediary bank processing and currency conversion.


### How do I track a wire transfer that hasn't arrived yet?


Request your tracking reference directly from the sending bank: for domestic transfers, ask for the IMAD/OMAD number, which locates the transaction within the Federal Reserve clearing network; for international SWIFT transfers, ask for the UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference). A completed status on the sender's dashboard confirms the instructions were transmitted, but intermediary banks can still delay the final credit to the recipient's account.
